hook: He ran the Olympic marathon with no shoes. And beat every shoe on Earth.
story: Rome, 1960. Abebe Bikila, a captain in Ethiopia's palace guard, lines up for the Olympic marathon. His new shoes had given him blisters - so he decided to run barefoot, on cobblestones. The race starts at night, with soldiers holding torches along the route. And the course passes a stolen monument: the obelisk Mussolini's army had looted from Ethiopia, twenty years before. Right beside it, the barefoot guard begins his final sprint.
number: He finishes in 2 hours, 15 minutes, 16.2 seconds - a new world record, barefoot. Ethiopia's first Olympic champion in history.
closer: And he was just getting started. Follow for part two.
